exposure: mode of delivery (pre-labor cesarean section, in-labor cesarean section, vaginal delivery)
outcome: levels of inflammatory markers (IL-18, MCP-1, CRP, sTNF RI)
levels of neurotrophic factors (BDNF, NT-3, S100B)
cohort: Newborns from the CODIBINE study, divided into three groups after delivery mode: pre-labor cesarean section (n = 714), in-labor cesarean section (n = 655), and vaginal delivery (n = 5,897)
finding: Neonatal levels of inflammatory and stress markers were significantly lower, while levels of growth factors were higher, after pre-labor cesarean section compared to vaginal delivery, while biomarker levels were similar after in-labor cesarean section and vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The study found that neonatal levels of inflammatory and stress markers were significantly lower after pre-labor cesarean section compared to vaginal delivery, while levels were similar after in-labor cesarean section and vaginal delivery.
